name: Google Gemini Developer API pricing (serverless, per 1M tokens, 2026-10-04 list price)
region: Google AI Studio / Gemini Developer API, global endpoint
price_basis: USD per 1M TOKENS, LIST PRICE, observed 2026-10-04, page last updated 2026-10-01 UTC. Gemini 3.8 Flash Standard tier: input $0.75, output $3.75, context-caching reads $0.075, all through December 31 2026 - each of those DOUBLES on January 1 2027 to $1.50 / $7.50 / $0.15. Same model, other tiers: Batch $0.375 in / $1.875 out; Flex $0.375 in / $1.875 out; Priority $1.35 in / $6.75 out. price_usd = Standard input. Explicit storage charge on the page: context-caching STORAGE is $0.50 per 1M tokens PER HOUR through 2026-12-31, doubling to $1.00 from 2027-01-01 - a per-hour recurring charge on cached context, not a one-off write. Grounding add-ons: Google Search and Maps 5,000 free requests per month shared across Gemini 3.x, then $14 per 1,000 requests; embeddings for File search $0.15 per 1M tokens. The identical Standard/Batch/Flex numbers appear on Gemini 3.7 Flash and 3.6 Flash, i.e. the Flash tier is priced as one band regardless of generation.
notes:
A DATE-BOUND PRICE WITH A PUBLISHED CLIFF IS THE MOST DANGEROUS KIND TO CACHE, AND THIS IS ONE. Every Gemini 3.x Flash figure on this page is explicitly 'through December 31, 2026' with a stated doubling 'starting January 1, 2027'. Any comparison written today is only valid for the remainder of 2026 and a reader in 2027 who trusts a stored $0.75 will be wrong by exactly 2x. Note also that Batch and Flex are priced IDENTICALLY here (both $0.375 in / $1.875 out) whereas at OpenAI Flex and Batch are also equal but at a different multiplier - do not assume the tiers are portable between vendors. Second structural point: this is the only provider in this set that prices cached-context STORAGE explicitly and per hour, which for a large stable prefix can dominate the token bill. Google publishes no GPU hourly rate for its Gemini serving fleet.

 EXPORT CONTROL (2026-10-04): NOT APPLICABLE IN THE HARDWARE-SHIPMENT SENSE - this record prices a token-based API, so no accelerator is transferred across a border and the ECCN 3A090 hardware licence regime does not attach to the transaction. Recorded null rather than false precisely because a token API is where export control instead becomes an END-USER/TERMS question: the provider applies geographic and end-user restrictions to service access (the AI Diffusion Rule briefly put a tiered country structure on exactly this kind of service before being rescinded on 2025-05-13), and a customer can still be refused under sanctions or end-use policy regardless of where the compute sits. Anyone reading this record for a restricted destination should look at the provider's terms, not at the EAR. Sources for the regime: spl-bis-2025-05-ai-diffusion-rescission, spl-bis-2026-05-d5-guidance.

 LEAD TIME: null - correct and not a gap. A token-priced serverless API is provisioned on request, so there is no lead time to publish; the binding constraint when a model is at capacity is provider-side queuing and any per-account concurrency limit, which this repo records in notes where a vendor publishes one (see the DeepSeek concurrency figures already here). Deliberately NOT recorded: any 'model capacity lead time' estimate, because vendors publish none and the SEO 'GPU lead time' numbers that circulate do not apply to a rented endpoint. Probe log in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time.

 STALENESS FLAG added 2026-10-04, and this one is time-boxed in a way the others are not: every Gemini 3.x Flash rate in price_basis is explicitly 'through December 31 2026' with a PUBLISHED DOUBLING on January 1 2027 ($0.75 -> $1.50 input, $3.75 -> $7.50 output, cache read $0.075 -> $0.15, and context-cache STORAGE $0.50 -> $1.00 per 1M tokens per hour). So this record's stored price is correct today and wrong by exactly 2x in under three months - the shortest validity window of any priced record in data/supply. A reader who trusts the stored $0.75 after 2026-12-31 is wrong by 2x. The stored figures are the through-2026 tier and must not be silently read as the 2027 tier; anyone modelling beyond 2026 should apply the published doubling rather than assume it.
